correctness.rationale: For uniform matchings of 2n labeled points on a convex circle, reconstructed s^S=product over all 2n boundary-adjacent potential chords [1+(s-1)I_e]. Only endpoint-disjoint marked boundary chords can coexist; such chords cross no other chords and their removal preserves the entire crossing statistic of the remaining cyclically ordered endpoints. Exactly c_{n,k}=2n/(2n-k)*binom(2n-k,k) k-edge matchings of C_{2n} exist, giving the full polynomial sum c_{n,k}(s-1)^k T_{n-k}(q). The single/double simple-chord inclusion probabilities and the standard Touchard–Riordan crossing second moment give ES, VarS, EX, VarX and Cov(S,X)=-2n(n-1)/[3(2n-1)]; division yields Corr=-sqrt(5/(n+3)) for every n>=2, including perfect negative correlation at n2. Independently enumerated all 3,15,105,945,10,395,135,135 matchings for n2..7 and checked each of the five exact moment identities. The unrestricted generating-polynomial identity has an all-size marked-deletion proof independent of these counts.
residual_risks: Uses a classical crossing-variance formula correctly credited to the Touchard–Riordan/Flajolet–Noy literature; enumeration stops at n7. Cyclic adjacency includes the boundary pair 1,2n, unlike open linear short-chord variants.

value.rationale: A joint exact enumerator and negative-correlation identity for two natural but structurally distinct statistics are useful beyond either classical marginal. The marked-chord deletion method gives all conditional crossing laws for designated nonintersecting boundary chords, and the simple closed correlation shows a concrete local-to-global dependence at every n.
